title: Fix the pipeline whose consumers never end

task.text: `Pipeline.process` never returns: its consumers wait for work that will never come.
Fix `Pipeline` so `process(amounts, consumers)` returns the sum of all amounts once every consumer thread has finished.

items: Keep `process(List<Integer>, int)`, the `Job` record and the bounded `BlockingQueue<Job>`.
Every consumer must exit by itself: do not interrupt them and do not poll with timeouts.
A real amount may be `0` or negative, so the end signal must not be confused with a real job.

checks.title: Every amount is summed and process returns
No amounts: consumers stop, total is 0
Zero and negative amounts are real jobs

hints.text: A consumer blocked in `take()` cannot tell "the producer is slow" from "the producer is done". The queue is the only channel between them, so the end of the work has to travel through it.
After the last real job, put one stop marker on the queue per consumer. A consumer that takes the marker leaves its loop. Compare with `==` against a single shared `Job` instance, not by value.
In the producer and the consumer:

lines: private static final Job STOP = new Job(0);
for (int c = 0; c < consumers; c++) queue.put(STOP);
